summary: This bill requires the Secretary of State to establish an Initiative on Foreign Investment Screening to provide technical assistance, training, and advisory services to foreign countries to help them screen foreign investments for national security risks.

scores.thoughts: This bill aims to strengthen foreign investment screening mechanisms in partner countries to protect against national security risks, which includes supply chain vulnerabilities. While not directly about tariffs or free trade agreements, it influences the conditions under which foreign investment (a component of international trade) occurs, promoting more secure and resilient supply chains. The bill defines 'partner country' to include those with which the U.S. has free trade agreements, indicating an intent to secure existing trade relationships rather than restrict them.

The bill establishes an Initiative on Foreign Investment Screening to provide technical assistance, training, and advisory services to foreign countries. This constitutes a form of non-monetary foreign aid aimed at capacity building in investment security, which is a central function of the bill.
